articleTitle: Designing For Immortality
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Electrical surges from lightning and power utility fluctuations frequently damage equipment powered from the AC line. We discuss the actual surge environment, based on the analysis of a large installed base of commercial surge protectors .

articleTitle: 40 W Integrated Car Radio Audio Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a BTL (Bridge Tied bad) class-H, high -power, high-efficiency audio amplifier for car radio applications. With a supply of 14.4 V, the output power is 40 W into an 8 /spl Omega/ load this is not possible using a normal class-B amplifier. Assuming that the music signal at the input has a normal (Gaussian) amplitude disrnbution, the dissipation is about 50% less than that of a class-B BTL amplifier with the same output power.

articleTitle: An Electronic Zoom Video Camera Using Imager Scanning Control
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An electronic zmm system forvida camera use was developed. Zoom Ratios were designed to be smoothly changd vertically and horizontally by controlling imager scanning and line memory scanning respectively.

articleTitle: Solving Home Automation Problems using artificial Intelligence Techniques
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The most difficult problem facing the success of future consumer borne automation products is not a purely technical one: how to make the products or systems intuitive to use, work together, yet powerful enough to have real perceived value to the consumer. The paper describes how existing Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques are directly applicable to solving the human interface problem of home automation products even when the" system intelligence" is widely distributed among different products sharing a common home network.

articleTitle: A Study On Trick Plays For Digital VCR
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Approaches to high speed play in digital VCR with a bit rate reduction are described. Discrete Cosine Transform ( DCT ) and Variable Length Coding (VLC) are adopted for the bit rate reduction. In order to make the degradation of picture quality as small as possible in high speed play) we developed data quantity control by the unit of sync block, compression block forming method and data format in the sync block.

articleTitle: A Digital Servo Signal Processing LSI For Compact Disc Players
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A new 5 V IF PLL for VIF-/SIF-signal detection in TV sets and VTR's
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This presentation introduces a new 5 V IC which uses PLL techniques for vision- and sound-lF signal processing in TV sets and VTRS. The functional content of the P-2 and the technique of the two independent PLL demodulators for video and sound signals are described. Finally, a comparison is made with state-of-the-art IF demodulators.

articleTitle: Advanced multistandard TV-sound IF integrated circuit
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new bus controlled multistandard sound IF IC is presented. The main functional blocks, which are lF-amplifier with AGC, IF-PLL, local oscillator generation, integrated filters and FM demodulators with automatic alignment and I*C bus control, will be discussed.

articleTitle: Appliance design for home automation
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new model for appliance design, called the "distributed appliance," is proposed. Distributed appliance operate in conjunction with a home automation communications network. Thk model is contrasted to present appliance design. The features of thw model and the benefits to consumers and manufacturers are explored.

articleTitle: A Digital Video Camera With An Arbitrary Aspect Ratio
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A novel video camera with an arbitrary aspect ratio was successfully developed by using newly-developed digital signal processing VLSIs. And it became possible to produce not only wide-screen pictures but also intentional fat and slim 3:4 pictures.

articleTitle: A Multi-channel PCM Sound Receiver For Satellite Broadcasting
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A prototype common indoor receiving unit for the two similar multi-channel PCM sound broadcasting systems that respectively use the broadcasting satellite and the communication satellite in the 12 GHz band, has been developed. The features of the receiver are such that advanced technologies such ss the high-speed Viterbi soft decision and the MSK (Minimum Shift Keying) demodulator are adopted.

articleTitle: One Chip Digital Servo For Compact Disc
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This chip provides all servo functions in a two stage CD system. The servo characteristics are widely adjustable through a serial interface and there are no external adjust ments necessary. The circuit is optimized for low power/voltage applications.

articleTitle: A Real-time Implementation Of Key VSELP Routines on a 16-bit DSP Chip
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper dkcusses a teal-time implementation of the Vector Sum-Excited LhsearPredictive WSELP) stx?ech coder which hm tin chosen as the digital cellular st&dard ~ North America and Japan. A real-time implementation of the VSELP algorithm cars be reaMzed using a Motorola digital signat processor, the DSP56 156. The principles of the VSELP algorithm, the real-time implementation of the algorithm on the DSP56 156, aud finite word-length effects are considered in the following discussion.

articleTitle: A Standard Multipurpose Fax Processor
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A standard multipurpose FAX processor has been developed for information system application. The facsimile and flow control functions previously distributed between several chips have been integrated orI a single chip, enabling easy addition of the facsimile function to various terminals.

articleTitle: Commercial Echo Canceller For Television
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Cancellation of television ghost images promises to improve the quality of NTSC reception. However, receivers with cancellation abilities can not be used until the broadcasters transmit a requisite reference signal. This paper will describe some ghost cancellation systems, will touch on the issues that go into a choice for such a reference signal and describe preliminary results of field tests with two such reference signals.

articleTitle: A-complete Single Supply Dual 18-bit Audio DAC
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A complete 18-bit dual voltage-out audio DAC was developed on a 2-/spl mu/m BICMOS process. It operates from a single 5V supply for 50-mW power dissipation and achieves 0.004% THD+Noise, 97.5dB SNR, and 115dB channel separation. The die measures 2.65x3.43 2 mm/sup 2/.

articleTitle: The Digital Spectrum-compatible HDTV Transmission System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Real-time Pitch (frequency) Shifting Techniques
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A technique for generating an interpolated signal for frequency (pitch) shifting applications is the topic of this paper, which covers the filtering algorithm used to generate the coefficients needed to interpolate samples in realtime, the speed of the algortibm in terms fo instructions cycles on the Motorola DSP56001 digitat signat processor, and a comparison of parameters affecting the signal to total harmonic distortion + noise ratio (STHDNR).

articleTitle: High Quality MUSE-NTSC converter LSIs
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Video Signal Processing And Memory-based Features
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A bew system architecture with analog YUV and HV interfaces is presented. The architecture allows easy implementation of memory-based features in highly specified TV sets. Integrated circuits and memory-based features which fit into this architecture are discussed.

articleTitle: Digital Compact Cassette
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Lower Shifting FM Carrier Recording In HD VCR For Baseband\muse Signals
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Zero Peripheral Secam Decoder
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A fully-integrated SECAM decoder will be described in which the SECAMcloche filter, a PLL FM demodulator, the identification circuit, and a low-frequency reemphasis filter have been combined. The circuit is alignment-free and requires only two peripheral capacitors.

articleTitle: Beyond1/spl mu/m/sup 2/ high density recording with improved QAM technique
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new QAM (Quadrature Amplitude Modulation) recording technique developed for digital VCRS is reported here. By using an improved coded 16-QAM method, a recording density as high as 0.95 /spl mu/m/sup 2/ /bit is accomplished on a conventional ME (Metal Evaporated) tape.

articleTitle: Error Control Codes For Advanced Television Signals Based Upon Preliminary And Post Filtering
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Several aspects of the design of filters for burst error control for television signals in new or existing, analog or digital formats wili be described. The error control capability is provided by prefiltering, so no redundant information need be transmitted. Prefilters which minimize distortion of the image and optimize effectiveness in estimating errors will be discussed. Postfilters which can compensate for the prefiltering, further minimizing the small distortion are discussed. These error control methods can implement very efficient real-number outer codes that provide burst or impulse noise protection for signals in digital format that may employ standard finite-field inner codes, data compression algorithms, and other digital or analog processing. This inner processing can exacerbate impulse noise or cause substantial burst errors, which should be removed by outer codes, such as the described ones, in order to achieve the desired subjective improvement of advanced television.

articleTitle: A 10-bit 60 MHz EPROM trimming DAC
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A 10-bit 60MHz DAC (digital-to-analog converter) has heen developed with Bi-CMOS process. This device has achieved 0. 15 LSB accuracy applying new EPROM trimming technique at 60MHZ operation which automatically read out trimming data, stored in EPROM.

articleTitle: The Photo CD System: An Overview For Consumer And Photofinishing
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The Photo CD system links traditional still photography with post-capture electronic still and computer based imaging. Three environments are considered; photofinishing, home viewing, and computerized image processing. A technical overview of system components and their interrelationships is presented.

articleTitle: A Low Smear Structure For 2M-pixel CCD Image Sensors
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed a new smear suppression cell structure built with the second Al shunt process, for 1-inch optical format 2M-pixel FIT-CCD image sensors. The characteristics of this structure are that the first Al layer works as the photoshield and the second one is used for the V-register drive pulse wiring. With this structure, we could reduce smear levels to less than -110dB. Moreover, we could achieve levels below -120dB with a micro on-chip-lens.

articleTitle: Multi-picture System For High Resolution Wide Aspect Ratio Screen
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new LSI chip set for multi-picture function has been developed. An aspect ratio conversion processor and a picture in picture processor achieved a multi-picture function of a wide aspect ratio screen.

articleTitle: A Voice Activated Car Audio System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed a new speech detection technology called Enhanced Level-Adaptive Segmentation method (ELASE method). ELASE method can distinguish driver's commands from audio sounds. Using the ELASE method, we have developed a voice activated car audio system. The proof of ELASE method's accuracy is its ability to operate car audio systems when car audio system is playing.

articleTitle: A Robust Approach To Tele-control Using DTMF signaling
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: New transfer equipment is being developed whose mode can be changed by touch tone. This paper describes a double touch tone-DTMF- monitoring method using the statistical characteristics of a touch tone decorder for a holding tone.

articleTitle: Microcontroller Compatible Clock Chip Design Using Field Programmable Gate Array
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a microcontroller compatible real time clock chip design using Field Programmable Gate Array. The relatively short cycle time to develop a product from concept to final chip is described.

articleTitle: DBS Program Distribution Network in Local Area through Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Described is a new optic-fiber audio/video signal transmission system for distributing the DBS programs to the displays/receivers in a local area where there is no enough space to install antennas for each receiver. A customer who has a DBS receiver but no space for setting an antenna can receive the DBS programs through the optical fiber system. A customer who has no DBS receiver can also receive the DBS programs by a video display through the optical fiber system. The DG/DP of the transmission system for a video signal was under 4 % and 3 degrees. The distortion factor for an audio signal was under 0.08 % in mode A and 0.02 % in mode B, respectively. The SNR of a video signal was above 40 dB (unweight) and SNR for an audio signal was above 60 dB in mode A and 70 dB in mode B.

articleTitle: A New Video Coding Algorithm And The Multimedia System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: An advanced audio signal processor
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: lThis paper describes an advanced floatingpoint Digital Signal Processor and ifs application to high-end professional and consumer audio market. The DSP prow'des a cost effective solution to such applications as PC MultiMedia, Graphic Equalizers, high precision FIR and IIR filters, and high quality audio encoder and decoders suitable for digital TV applications.

articleTitle: Computer-aided generation of video test signals for simulation of television systems
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The present article shows how computer assisted-drafting and computer assisted engineering programs can be used effectively in otrder to generate TV test signals to evaluate and design television systems and facilities. An on the shelf computer design package , together with a properly adapted drafting program are extensively used in this work to simulate a combination of TV test signal generator, circuit modeling tool, waveform monitor and measurement set. The computer model described here enables the engineer to analyze the effects of a specific TV system on video test signals, without the expense of using an actual test generator. Examples of linear and non linear distortions, produced by specific circuit systems on generated TV test signals are given and analyzed in the time and frequency domain , respectively. Finally, a brief discussion about the package advantages offered by the application of the selected computer simulation package in the design and testing of TV circuit systems is presented.

articleTitle: The Bubble Operating System: A Control Extension To Data Flow Diagram
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper there is described a control system extension for software specification and design using Structured Analysis for Real Time ( SA/RT ) technique. Described method makes it possible to have computer assisted binding between the 5A model and the code. This binding is carried out with a small real time operating system concept BOSS.

articleTitle: Ghost Canceler LSI Kit For TV Set
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Recently, High quality picture TVs such as ACTV, EDTV, and HDTV are widely discussed. One of the improvement picture degradation in over-the-air television (ground-wave) is the reduction of ghost interference that results from the multipath propagation created as the reflection or scatter of the transmitted signal from buildings or mountains, etc. Ghosts are multiple images being overlaid along with the original image on the TV receiver. We have successed in developing an LSIS (picture 1) for a ghost canceler (see fig. 1) in Japan.

articleTitle: High Density Muse Videodisc
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed a MUSE (Multiple Sub-Nyquist Sampling Encoding) videodisc with 60 minutes of playback time per side of CLV disc. The recording density of the disc is doubled as that of NTSC videodisc. And the visible laser diode with a wavelength of 670 nm and an objective lens with an N.A. (numerical aparture) of 0.6 are used for playing the disc. As a result, a fine playedback image was obtained as reported herein.

articleTitle: The European Broadcasting Union's Programme Delivery Control System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Programme Delivery Control (PDC) is a data broadcasting service which provides viewer-friendly control of home video recording. Suitably-equipped VCRS record preselected programmed automatically and completely, in spite of any changes made by broadcasters to their published schedules. A common data structure may be used with all television signals, whether delivered by terrestrial broadcast, cable or direct from satellite.

articleTitle: A Compatibly Improved VHS System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A compatibly impmved VHS system that gives performance similar to S-VHS is described. The additional bandwidth of the luminance signal is obtained by a spatio/temporal subsampling method, which results in folding of the frequencies so that the entirre 4.2 MIIz signal can be carried within the standard 2.5 MHz band of the WS luminance signal.

articleTitle: A Digital Video Equalizer For Cancelling Transmission Distortion
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Automatic Viewing Range Tracing Method For Communication Equipment
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Automatic viewing range tracing (AVRT) feature by which the field of vision automatically traces the person in front of a camera, has been developed for still picture video telephone sets and video doorphones etc. A new algorithm and LSI have been developed to achieve this feature. Also developed is a video doorphone adopting this new feature.

articleTitle: Horizontal Deflection Processor For Wide Range Self-adaptive monitor
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a new self-adaptive horizontal processor, which can work in a continuous and automatic way over a very wide range of frequencies (10 to 120 KHz) covering almost all the existing standards. The chip is self-adaptive in the sense that it does not require any external adjustment to lock the incoming sync whichever is the frequency and the duty-cycle.

articleTitle: VHS-improved Reproduction By Using Active Phase Shift
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The evolution of video recorders has lead to new techniques in signal processing. With the active phase shift circuit, a video playback system for VHS-standard has been created that guarantees a dramatic improvement in picture quality, even for highly stressed tapes, while keeping the full compatibility to the VHS-standard. This is realized by an active control of phase shifting: The upper FM carrier sideband-lost in the magnetic recording process - is reproduced in its original form. Low noise and high resolution, the opposing parameters relevant to picture quality, can thus both be regained to their mawimurn specifications. Apart from the phase shift, signal sparks and noise are suppressed by a level-dependant band pass, filtering the disturbed FM signal parts.

articleTitle: An Interpolator For HD-MAC decoder
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In the 3-branch HD-MAC system, blocks of the picture are prefiltered and subsampled according to motion modes: stationary, slow motion, and fast motion. This paper describes an interpolator for HDMAC decoder using a combinations of some simple filters and a method to interpolate pixels across blocks of different sampling structures.

articleTitle: A New DC-controlled And DC-coupled Monitor Deflection Concept
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Two integrated circuits and a few peripheral components are used to implement the horizontal small signal processing and the entire vertical signal processing for a VGA-monitor. Using DC.controlled adjustments and signal processing improves the petformence, reduces the component count, simplifies the monitor design and is necessary for computercontrolled applications.

articleTitle: Study On The Interchangeability Of The VTR
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: New measuring methods for tape running stability and track straightness were developed, by which realtime and high precise observation of tape motion on helix guide of drum was achieved, thus optimum mechanical conditions were decided, resulting in good interchangeability.

articleTitle: Detecting The Audible Alarm Of Residential Smoke Detectors And Its Applications
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Technology has been developed to provide a practical wireless alarm interconnection between residential smoke detectors and supplemental safety warning devices. Digital signal processing detects the unique signal "signature" of the smoke detector's audible alarm and automatically activates the warning devices. There is broad compatibility with existing smoke detectors, No changes or additions are required to tens of millions of residential smoke detectors already installed worldwide.

articleTitle: Development Of A Dolby S-type IC using new master slice method
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An audio signal processing lC for the Dolby Stype consumer audio noise reduction system has been developed using a new bipolar mastex slice process with high flexibility

articleTitle: A High-speed Neural Analog Circuit For Computing The Bit-level Transform Image Coding
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a Hopfield-type neural network approach which leads to an analog circuit for implementing the bit-level transform image. Different from the conventional digit al approach to image coding, the analog coding system would operate at a much higher speed and require less hardware than digital system. In order to utilize the concept of neural net, the computation of a two-dimensional DCT-based transform coding should be reformulated as minimizing a quadratic nonlinear programming problem subject to the corresponding 2's complement binary variables of 2-D DCT coefficients. A novel Hopfield-t ype neural net with a number of graded-response neurons designed to perform the quadratic nonlinear programming would lead to such a solution in a time determined by RC time constants, not by algorithmic time complexity. A fourth order Runge-Kutt a simulation is conducted to verify the performance of the proposed analog circuit. Experiments show that the circuit is quite robust and independent of parameter variations and the comput ation time of 8 x 8 DCT is about ins. In practice, programmable hybrid digital-analog MOS circuits are required to implement the neural-based DCT optimizer. The circuit techniques are based on extremely simple and programmable analog parameterized MOS modules with such attractive features as reconfigurability, input/output compatibility, and unrestricted fan-in/fan-out capability.

articleTitle: Full Digital C.cxwergence System For HDTV
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new digital convergence system for HD/NTSC compatible TV has been developed. A convergence waveform generator IC and a calculation algorithm achieved an 8 seconds automatic alignment using minimum input data. The algorithm also converts HDTV system data to NTSC one.

articleTitle: TDSD2 - A Highly Integrated Decoder For Nicam-728
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Domestic load management system using power line carrier
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a new domestic load management system. We have designed this system for already-built-houses which wired 200 volt one-phase three-wire system.

articleTitle: Switch Mode Power Supply, New Concept
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new power supply concept is described. Using the main transformer to transfer the secorrdary regulation signal on a primary winding, a new developed IC controls the primary and secondary voltages to provide more protection in case of disturbance.

articleTitle: Adaptive DPCM With Median Type Predictors
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an improved DPCM (Differential pulse Code Modulation) coding method that utilizes adaptive quantization and nonlinem (median type) predictors (Median Adaptive DPCM, MADPCM). DPCM is a promising coding method for television applications because of its simplicity and visual properties. The simulation results of the MADPCM coder obtained with the DVSR 100 digital video sequencer indicate that good picture quality can be achieved with a compression ratio of 2.7:1 (3 bits/pixel).

articleTitle: NICAM Decoder For Digital Multi-channel TV Sound Broadcast
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: CD-quality Digitally Controlled TV Stereo Sound Processor
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Digital TV-sound standards such as NICAM and D2-MAC now offer CD-equivalent sound quality. The single-chip TV-soundprocessor described below combines CD quality sound processing for both loudspeaker and headphone connections combined with an extremely low error probability of the pilot decoder. It is controlled via a bidirectional serial bus interface.

articleTitle: A New Noise Reduction System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A video camera noise reduction system capable of an S/N improvement of 9 dB of color difference signal is developed. In this system, the video signals are transformed into spatial frequency components to which feedbacks are discriminatively applied.

articleTitle: A 1" Format 1.5M Pixel IT-CCD Image Sensor For An HDTV Camera System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A 1" format 1.5M pixels IT-CCD image sensor has been developed for an HDTV camera system. To achieve high performances we have adopted a novel impurity profile of buried Pi-layer and an onchip micro lens array. We have obtained high fidelity pictures with a horizontal resolution of 820 TV lines.

articleTitle: PVC-1: Photo CD video controller ASIC
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The PVC-1 was developed in order to provide a number of user features in consumer and commercial grade Photo CD players. It accepts decoded data in the Photo CD format from a CD player mechanism, stores it into a conventional 256K x 16 DRAM using one of eight selectable modes, and reads it from the DRAM to generate video rasters in either M-NTSC or B-PAL formats. An interface for an external eight bit microcontroller is included for passing control and status information and to allow certain types of non-Photo CD data to be passed from the CD player to the microcontroller.

articleTitle: The GSM mobile station - Realisation of the consumer handheld model
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The paper describes the GSM mobile telephone system with focus on a low-cost, handheld model of the mobile station. By using full custom ASICS the price of the mobile station will be acceptable for the consumer market.

articleTitle: A Study On Enhancement Signals And Transmission Spaces For Advanced TV
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The relationship between signals for enhancement and the spaces in Advanced TV is examined from various standpoints, such as moving/stationary properties of main signals and multiplexed signals, and the correlation of these signals. Some schemes are suggested, and an experimental proto-model for a letter-box method has been implemented.

articleTitle: A New Simulation System For Video Signals
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed a new simulation system for video signal processing circuits, which solves the

articleTitle: A low-power switchingresonance-driving method for HDTV CCD image sensors
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new low-power switch ing-resona rice-driving method suitable for HDTV two-million-pixel CCD image sensors is described. The operational anlysis and experimental results have clarified the behaviour of this driving method.

articleTitle: An Edge Detection Approach To Digital Image Stabilization Based On Tri-state Adaptive Linear Neurons
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new approach to digital image stabilization for video cameras is proposed by using an edge detection method, which is based on tr-state adaptive linear neurons (ADALlNES) [1]. The proposed image stabilizing system efficiently reduces image fluctuation effects caused by human hand instability.

articleTitle: Full motion on CD-I
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Full motion will extend CD-I with the capability to play moving natural pictures on full screen with associated audio of C~Digital-Audio quality. Ml CD-I discs with full motion will be playable in both a 50 Hz player and a 60 Hz player. In the paper, a description of the full motion system is given.

articleTitle: Low-noise, Low-distortion Front-end IC For 1.1 -V Paging Receiver
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A Motion Insensitive Method For Scan Rate Conversion And Cross Error Cancellation
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new motion insensitive method for scan rate conversion and removing cross errors from video signal is presented. It is based on the recently introduced vector median concept. In the developeds ystem beth scan rate conversion and cross error cancellation use common image memories and can be implemented by the same filtering circuit.

articleTitle: Performance Of C-MAC VSAT Data Services
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper considers the transmission of C-MAC data services to VSATS. The effects of adjacent satellite interference and low gain are evaluated in terms of the received bit error rate and its implication for coding for typical data services.

articleTitle: Managing Secure and Confidential Video Distribution
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Consumers and small companies are increasingly producing and reproducing video tapes. This paper looks at means to utilize video tapes for secure communication of confidential information within companies or related business sectors.

articleTitle: A 12 Band Microprocessor Controlled Graphic Equalizer Display filter IC
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A 12-Band microprocessor controlled graphic equalizer display filter IC, dedicated for use in audio applications is described. The device is implemented in a 2 micron CMOS process and utilizes switched capacitor technology to replace several discrete components (op amps, resistors, capacitors, diodes) and multiplexer. The chip occupies 18,000 square roils and dissipates 100 mw.

articleTitle: An Analog BiCMOS Integrated Circuit For Front-end RDS Decoder
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Line Rate Upconversion In IDTV Applications
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Median based and linear algorithms have been developed for interpolating 625 extra lines between 625 original lines in PAL receiver. Some algorithms are excellent for moving areas and others for still areas. Motion detection has been used in order to utilize different algorithms on still and moving areas.

articleTitle: A Broadband Customer Premises Network Prototype For Integrated Communications Services
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A broadband customer premises network (CPN) provides communications and control interface functions between public information networks and among customer terminal equipment. In this paper, we describe an experimental research prototype CPN designed to interconnect with future public exchange telecommunications networks, where access may be provided via optical fiber to or near the premises, in digital format and at information rates far in excess of those currently proviided by today's telephone systems.

articleTitle: Complex-valued ghost cancellation reference
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new Ghost Cancellation Reference (GCR) signal has been proposed for TV broadcasting, the complex-valued GfJR (CVGCR). The CVGCR has many advantages compared to the BTA's GCR and the GCR of a Pseudo Random Sequence.

articleTitle: CEBus router testing
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A prototype CEBUS router has been developed to gather performance data for the EfA standard. Testing evaluated the tradeoffs in throughput and delay, as well as the amount of overhead trafllc requtred to maintain the network topology.

articleTitle: Multistandard Video Front-end
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This presentation will describe a high.pedomance multistandard colour decoder IC which is alignment-free and capable of decoding TVcolour signals which are transmitted in accordance with any of the standards in use throughout the world. All the filters for the chroma circuits are integrated and very few peripheral components are needed.

articleTitle: A Facsimile Broadcasting Receiver
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A fats imile broadcasting receiver has been developed which is compatible with the Group 3 facsimile in both its transmitting and receiving functions. The receiver has a thermal transfer printer and a high resolution LCD. Therefore both hard and soft copies are available.

articleTitle: System And Application Management In A Homenetwork
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A difficult (but important) task of a home network is to manage and configure the resources attached to the network. This paper describes how the ESPRIT Home System allows this to be achieved in a flexible way with a minimum of user intervention.

articleTitle: Wide band GaAs IC for DBS/TV receiver
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A Wide band GaAs, IC which can receive TV/CATV channels and Broadcasting Satellite channels is newly designed. This GaAs IC makes the size of tuner unit compact with satisfactory characteristics.

articleTitle: Low Peripheral Multistandard TV Processor
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An economy l-chip multistandmd colour TV set will be described in which various functions (e.g. chroma filters and luminance delay line) have been integrated. The entire circuit requires only one adjustment.

articleTitle: Physical And Media Specifications Of The CXBus
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The lack of appliance interoperability has hindered the growth of the home automation industry. CEBUS, a new standard for home automation now being released by the EIA, will provide compatible communication between consumer devices. The CEBUS concept allows interconnection of video generating devices such as VCRs and cameras with infrared remote control units, CATV converters, TV antennas, TV sets and other video appliances. This video communication is supported by the coaxial bus, or CXBUS. Those who design, install, maintain or repair video appliances will need to understand the CXBUS and its affect on their systems and customers.

articleTitle: A new play-back method for R-DAT sing "Non-tracking" signal processing
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: LSI kit for closed caption decoder system
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a newly designed LSI Kit for Closed Caption Decoder System.

articleTitle: Proposed Architecture For An Integrated LPC Speech Synthesis/microcomputer
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An enhanced architecture is proposed for an integrated LPC speech synthesizer/microcomputer. The new architecture will enable the chip to address a much wider variety of applications, reducing the cost of telephone answering machines, talking greeting cards, and many other speech products.

articleTitle: TV, FM Radio And Weather Band Receixer With Integrated Tuning
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Unique integration of double conversion stereo FM and weather band radio has been accomplished using the television tuner and an FM radio IC. TV tuner issues, choice of first IF frequency, weather band tuning and overall design and performance are discussed.

articleTitle: Plastic Optical Fiber Technology in Consumer Applications: Practical, Affordable, and Capable
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: An ISDN Terminal Adapter
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A terminal adapter complying with the Japanese INS Net 64 ISDN standard has been developed. The adapter is designed to connect existing data and analog terminals to the ISDN. The hardware and software design of the terminal adapter will be presented.

articleTitle: A Digital Implementation Of AM Stereo Decoding
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Digitat Signat Processing (DSP) techniques have been used to record and reproduce high qufllty digital sound on compact disks and digital audio tapes for audio entertainment systems. Incorporating DSP technology to improve the quality of AM (amplitude modtdation) and FM (frequency modulation) stereo radio reception is a nataml progression. This paper will only deal with the AM stereo problem sines the digital FM stereo problem has been resolved and demonstrated [1]. This paper will discuss Motorola Compatible Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (CQAM) AM stereo decoding and how it can be digitally implemented on a Motorola DSP56001. A complete description of CQAM decoding will be given including a brief overview of how the process can be performed digitatly.

articleTitle: High performance block conversion for broadband (862 MHZ) CATV networks
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: For the first time, high performance block converters are used to extend broadband (862MHz) CATV networks to lower density areas. Complex intermodulation signals are generated and their effects are minimizd by the choice of the local oscillator frequency.

articleTitle: A Support System For Analog Circuit Design With Hierarchical Library
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present a support system to design analog circuits with a hierarchical library, which will enable the analog LSI to be designed with the hierarchical approach. An application example is also provided,

articleTitle: Consumer Electronics Impact Of Fiber Optics
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Consumer electronics products such as television receivem and VCR's are designed to accept and operate on a Radio Frequency, RF, input. Conductors of RF energy, such as coaxial cable, are craft-friendly. The Cable Television Industry has found techniques which dramatically increase performance in a very cost effective manner while preserving the RF nature of the final feed to the consumer electronics products. A cable system with 1 GHz bandwidth will be completed this year. It will carry 150 channels to the subscriber. Subsequent implementation of digital video compression will extend the channel capacity to well over 350 channels.

articleTitle: High Resolution Still Picture Transmission System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A 64kbits/s high resolution still picture ISDN communication system capable of receiving and transmitting a 1024 x 1024 pixels still picture in approximately 13 seconds has been developed. IBM PC-AT and AX-PC compatible picture codec board and ISDN communication interface board have been designed for use with this system. The JPEG image coding algorithm is implemented for image compression to assure ISDN connectivity. In addition to high resolution stifl pictures, the system transmits portrait images of the user. This system can be used for a wide range of applications, including simple video conference systems.

articleTitle: EUROCRYPT, a successful conditional access system
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: EUROCRYPT is a conditional access system for broadband networks, it is used in Europe on the cable and satellite networks in association with the MAC broadcasting standards. It offers all the commercial modes that have been identified for Pay-TV, with additional functions. It is a simple, safe, evolutive and user-friendly system, entitlements are transmitted in the signal with a large capability. Its implementation uses smart card. Since it has been specified, in March 1989, its success increased, and we hope that it will become the reference system for enhanced and high-definition television systems.

articleTitle: A Dual Low-power Continuous Calibration D/A Converter (CC-DAC) For Digital Audio
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This presentation describes a dual 16-bit low power D/A converter which uses a continuous calibration technique to achieve a S/(THD+N) of 85 dB and a dynamic range of 95 dB. The converter is fabricated in a CMOS process, has a chip area of 3.6 mm2 and is available in an 8-pin SO or DIL package.

articleTitle: Color temperature Alignment Using Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The flexibility of vision systems has lead to their introduction in many areas of manufacturing. The use of CCD camera based systems for aligning the color temperature of video displays is one of these areas. An implementation is discussed.

articleTitle: The Action-state Diagram: A Compact Finite State Machine For User Interfaces
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper there is described the use of the Action-State diagrams in software development of user interface. Presented method is also used in system design of small embedded reactive systems. This method allows specification, design and coding phases to be combined with very communicative and formal notation.

articleTitle: Waveform Equalization For EDTV Systems using QAM
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A TV Analogue To Digital Conversion System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Bus Controlled Clock - Generator
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A line locked clock generation circuit for digital video processing systems with a digital line-PLL and a digital/analog clock-PLL, using a virtual frequency twice that of a crystal.

articleTitle: A bitstream D/A Converter For Top Grade Digital Audio
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A high-performance integrated bitstream D/A converter for top-grade digital audio equipment is presented. CrosstaIk and non-linearity are minimized by a fully differential 1-bit DAC fabricated in a BIMOS process, It features low-distortion (-105 dB) and a wide dynamic range (109 dB).

articleTitle: FEM Analysis Of The Interface Phenomena Of VCR Tape And Head
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Characteristics of performance of VCR is quite dependent on the phenomena occurring at `the interface (air film pressure on the head and tape deflection along the head) between magnetic tape and head. Since it is very difficult to measure experimentally the air-film pressure at the interface and deflection of the medium, an accurate computer simulations of great importance. We developed the computational method for simulating the behavior of a tape running along a rotating cylinder with a video head fixed to it. The flexible tape is modeled by a thin anisotropic shell and the air-film is treated by the modified Reynolds equation. The two sets of equation are coupled together in the FEM( Finite Element Method). The calculation result show a good agreement with experimental ones within an error of 7 %.

articleTitle: New achitecture of a ghost cancel system
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: By troughly arranging the number of bits and taps of the transversal filters, we were able to develop a ghost-cancel system that provided a great reduction the in size of the circuit and enabled the use of LSIs.

articleTitle: A Triple-port Field Memory For Digital Video processing
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An 848 K-bit integrated C-MOS dynamic RAM has been developed featuring three independently clocked 4-bit wide data ports, buffered real-time R/W transfer, serial address input and 400 Mbit/s data rate. The chip is suitable for advanced IDTV and lQTV processing.

articleTitle: A High Quality Digital HDTV Codec
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A Programmable Deflection Processor
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed a multi-standard vertical deflection processor which is composed of a microprocessing and a digital signal processing block. It is possible to obtain minimum deflection distortion for big screens and good vertical synchronization.

articleTitle: Predictive Block-matching Motion Estimation Schemes for Video Compression (Digest)
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new motion estirrration/compensation scheme for full-motion interframe video compression is proposed in this paper. The scheme is based on prediction of inter-block and inter-frame motion information using minimum absolute difference block matching and hence substantially increases tbe searching and computation efficiency. A comparison is also made widr the "optimal" full motion searching scheme for a standard test sequence.

articleTitle: Video Signal Processing LSI For Home VCRs
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a newly designed video single processing LSI chip for home VCRs.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation and cost of Decoders for Digital HDTV
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Implementing the proposals for simulcast digital HDTV in consumer hardware presents a new challenge to consumer electronics manufacturers. A study of the hardware complexity and cost impact of several proposed systems will be presented.

articleTitle: PTV Convergence Waveform analysis using computer simulation techniques
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Computer simulations of the yoke and optics of a PTV system were run to calculate the desired current waveforms for a convergence circuit. These waveforms were then decomposed into practical waveforms by a variety of optimization techniques.

articleTitle: A Second-generation Nicam 728 TV Digital Stereo Sound Decoder Using Customised Digital Signal Processing Techniques.
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a second generation decoder IC for Nicam 728 TV digital stereo sound, employing multiprocessor techniques for DQPSK demodulation and Nicam data demultiplexing. Benefits are significant component reduction, mtdtistandard operation and improved performance.

articleTitle: New Method For Variable Speed Playback For High Definition VCRs
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Many papers have been published on the development of 1/2" high definition (HD) VCRS, Bandwidth of the HDTV signal so wide that a multi-channel & multisegment recording method is employed for HD VCRS. In recent years, one of the main concerns of the recording method for HD VCRs has been how to realize variable speed playback. We developed a 1/2" HD VCR using the 2 channel 3 segment recording method. However, it has been pointed out that realization of variable speed playback in this recording method is very difficult. This paper describes a new method which enables the VCR to perform the noiseless variable speed playback.

articleTitle: Integration of CEBus with utility load management and automatic meter reading
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The writing of the CEBUS standard will provide utilities with exciting new concepts in load management and Automatic Meter Reading (AMR). It will be possible for homeowners to have an important influence in the load management responsibilities. As homeowners begin to purchase appliances outfitted with the CEBUS option, such as water heaters and air conditioners, utilities will be able to communicate with the appliance through a CEBUS meter. As a value added benefit to the utility for installing an intelligent meter, the utility will be able to obtain a monthly meter reading.

articleTitle: HDTV Signal Resolution Enhancement Near Moving Objects Using Motion And Boundary Detection
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The HD-MAC image is divided into 16*16 blocks, Moving objects are shown with lover resolution. The border blocks of the moving object include also non-moving background. Some non-moving blocks around the moving object are also erroneously coded with lower resolution. A method to enhance the resolution of the non-moving background with the help of picture memory is presented.

articleTitle: A Single Chip Audio Signal Processor For HDTV Receiver
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A Highly Integrated LSI For Nicam728 With Bi-CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new LSI for the NICAM728 (near-Instantaneously Companded Audio Multiplex at a rate of 728kbit/s[l]) has been developed. The LSI integrates almost the whole circuits to receive the NICAM stereo broadcasting. In this paper, we describe the LSI, stressing its features, functions and its advantages over the original IC set.

articleTitle: Pix-in-pix IC with digital decoding/encoding usin only clock
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper focuses on the unique aspects of a new pix-in-pix IC. The IC receives two composite video inputs and provides an overlayed composite video Output. All video decodinq and encodinq is performed in the IC usinq diqital siqnal processing. The IC uses a single clock.

articleTitle: A CCD Color Linear Image Sensor Employing New Transfer Method
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Development Of Compact inverter power supply for microwave oven
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes the development of an inverter Power supply for a microwave oven. The power SUPPLY featuring a fast switching device IGBT is light, compact, and able to control microwave output power.

articleTitle: Enhanced Authoring For CD-I
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Initial titles for multi-media systems such as Compact Disc Interactive were hand crafted by programmers. Now a range of softwme tools and run-time systems are becoming available which simplify the process of making entertaining consumer titles and return the skill to the designer.

articleTitle: Analog Signal Processor IC For Stereo Enhancement System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new IC for stereo enhancement system (Sound Retrieval System) has been developed. A single-chip analog signal processor achieved high performance, and reduced number of external components and size of the system.

articleTitle: computer aided error analysis for digital signal processing
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Computer aided analyses emphasize the importance of error amplitude distributions, error spectrum clue to quantization effects, and dynamic range accounting in revealing tradeoff relationships between data path, arithmetic implementation, and circuit topology.

articleTitle: Development Of Encorder IC For Video Cameras
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Encoder lC has been developed for colour video camera s. This IC includes many additional functions and its frequency bandwidth is `enough. It is useful for achieving higher quality pictures in "S-VHS" and "Hi8" format camcorders.

articleTitle: Photo CD And CD-I - A Marriage Of Great Convenience
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: New Multiplex/separation Schemes For Telecine Images
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Telecine images are special signals converted from film images, and the original frame rate is lower than that of ordinary TV signals. In this paper, two signal processing schemes for telecine images are proposed. These schemes are based on the technique of making a group of scan-lines which is synchronized with the original film frames. In these schemes, several signals can be transmitted without crosstalk while keeping compatibility with NTSC standards.

articleTitle: An Optimal Approach To Digital Raster Mapper Design
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An analytic method of digiti interpolator design is proposed. Performance approaching orequalling that of full polyphase filter designs is achieved through generation of orthogonal filters via singular value decomposition (SVD). This approach preserves the magnitude, group delay, and composite filter response.

articleTitle: Digital Realisation Of Phono (RIAA) Equalisers
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The paper presents a digital realisation of phono equalisers, using a simple first-order analogue pre-emphasis filter combined with a digital IIR type filter. This approach enables using a relatively simple digital filter while maintaining an accurate frequency response and a good dynamic range,

articleTitle: An Integrated Circuit Processor For A Multiple Scanning Antenna Diversity System For Mobile FM Reception
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: 2-H-adaptive combfiler video processor
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A muftistandard video processor for composite and S-VHS video signals is described. Based on a 2-H adaptive combfilter for PAL and NTSC, a horizontal and vertical peaking and a black-fevel-expander, the new circuit enhances the picture quality, by eliminating "crossalor" and "cross-luminance" artifacts and improving the two dimensional resolution and the contrast.

articleTitle: An Integrated Concept In Home Information Systems
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Videowav is a mass market general purpose telecommunication system for the delivery of television videoldata systems over existing cable-TV networks. Since December 1989, a commercial Videoway service has been introduced to Videotron cable subscribers with a potential of 1.6 million subscribers in Canada where the installed base is over 65,000 terminals and 1.2 million subscribers in the UK. This paper will concentrate on the functionalities of the multimedia Videoway technology and will be illustrated by a video presentation of the type of services now being providing to Videoway subscribers .

articleTitle: VideoCrypt An Open Architecture Pay TV System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This papers describes an open architecture Pay TV system using digital scrambling and secret algorithmic function encryption. It explains in detail the system scrambling and encryption techniques, the data transmission, and the system security features.

articleTitle: An Optimized Gateway Controller For Home Automation And Automatic Meter Reading System
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Gateway Controller connecting a Home Automation (HA) system with an Automatic Meter Reading system was developed. The Gateway Controller composed of modular lower and upper layer protocol translator between which an intermediate protocol was defined. Easy exchanges of the lower layer prokocol translator enable the Gateway Controller to adapt to any external network out of home. The Gateway Controller improves information-handling capability of the HA system.

articleTitle: Single-chip video processing system
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The entire video processing and controlling for a color TV has been developed on a single chip. Modular design and submicron technology allow the economic integration of features in all classes of TV sets. This paper outlines the characteristics of the system.

articleTitle: Development Of High-performance FM F.E. IC On Interference Characteristic
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: he Front End (F.E.) block is very important in determining the reception performance of car stereo FM tuners. We have developed a new AGC system for the FM F.E. that significantly suppresses interference and simplifies tuner design to satisfy market requirements.

articleTitle: A Study On The Method on Double The Data Rate For Recording/reproducing And Search Speed For DAT
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Method to double the data rate for recording/ reproducing and the search speed have been studied for high functional DAT. Both editting time , such as after-recording subcodes , and search time have been reduced by half

articleTitle: The Broadband Network Interface For Television
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The Public Video Switched Network, a demonstrator developed at GTE Laboratories Incorporated, illustrates a possible evolution of the local telephone network. This scenario provides end-to-end connections though highcapacity switched digital channels. Fiber-ready television receivers provide the network subscribers with a consumerfriendly digital interface to the network. The fiber-ready receivers have the potential to present a wide range of audio, data, and video services via a digital serial interface. The digital interface is one of four possible network connections to the fiber-ready television receiver. This digital interface provides the receiver with time-multiplexed audio, data, and video signals through a single 143-Mb/s serial bitstream. A 1200 baud control channel is provided out of the fiber-ready television for channel selection and interactive programming. The Public Video Switched Network supports a broadband topology that allows both broadcast and point-topoint networks direct access to the television receiver.

articleTitle: An Expanded Spanning-tree Protocol For Home-oriented Network Management
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Proposed here is an expanded spanning-tree protocol by which plural logical spanning-trees are simultaneously constructed in a network, and an extra packet traffic induced by a non-optimized routing path possible on a single fixed-tree can be prevented since each packet is routed through appropriate trees.

articleTitle: A World Standard Video And Sound IF IC
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An IC for wordwide video and sound IF applications is described below. It consists of: 1.) A video IF for positive and negative modulation with FPLL carrier regeneration followed by a video switch. A separate video output after the demodulator permits the installation of a sound trap at the input of the video switch. An AFC signal is derived from the VCO tuning voltage 2.) A sound IF for AM and FM sound transmission using a multi-standard FM IF converter. 3.) A dual FM sound IF for A2 stereo I dual sound transmission with A,M/FM audio switch at the audio output 1. 4.) An IZC bus interface controlling all switching functions and the three ports as well as for reading out the TV identification and the AFC data.

articleTitle: A Full Integrated Automatic Multistandard Chrona Decoder
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper discribes a new concept for an automatic multistandard chroma decoder . It includes an integrated double base band chroma delay line , and integrated biquad trap filters. This circuit , which provides complete multistandard chroma decoding without any external adjustment,is fully bus controled with a reply mode . SVHS Signals ,applied to the circuit, are automatically detected by the standard research cycles .It has been achieved in a double poly BICMOS 2um process . All the functions are imple-mented on a 20 mm2 dice and mounted in a shrinked 30 pins package .

articleTitle: Interoperability Of Consumer Control And Monitoring Networks Over The AC Powerline
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Multiple communications standards have been proposed for the home. The AC powerline offers an ideal backbone communications medium. This paper describes a powerline communications architecture that provides the required interoperability of these proposed standards.

articleTitle: Bit Rate Reduction Algorithm For A Digital VCR
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a bit rater eduction technology for use in digital VCRs, which is based on block scrambling and adaptive cosine transform codfng. In addition to block scrambling, a new simple and efficient variable-wordlength coding method is proposed.

articleTitle: A Study On The Digitization Of Audio Signals For S-VHS VCR
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The recording and reproducing characteristics , factors of interference , amendment against interference and performance against tracking error have been studied on digital audio system for S-VHS VCR. The block error rate of 5X 10-4 is attained without degradation of both video signal and FM audio signal,

articleTitle: Digital Audio Broadcast (DAB) Field Tests In Canada
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: During the summer and spring of 1990, field tests were performed in four Canadian Cities to study a new terrestrial Digital Audio Broadcast system proposed by the European EUREKA group. The system is particularly adapted to vehicular and urban reception.

articleTitle: New multipage teletext decoders
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Improved teletext services, limited transmission capacity and the reducing cost of the technology are all factors that are increasing the number of pages stored in teletext decoders. This paper describes two new decoders which use different techniques to achieve multipage capability.

articleTitle: Digitally Controlled Video Processor With Accurate Grey-scale
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A digitally controlled video processor with automatic CRT bias and video gain adjustment, contrast, saturation and brightness controls, and including a fast beam current limiter, has been designed from first principles to a specified grey-scale accuracy.

articleTitle: Fibre in the home
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: An Experimental Home-use Digital VCR With Three Dimensional DCT And Superimposed Error Correction Coding
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have newly developed an experimental home-use digital VCR system which adopted a three dimensional DCT coding for 4:2:2 digital component video signals and a superimposed error correction coding for very low redmrdancy.

articleTitle: An experimental digital VCR with new DCT-based bit-rate reduction system
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A high picture quality digital VCR was experimentally developed, using the triple ReedSolomon product code, a new block-coding technique with extensive lower frequency level suppression and a DCT-based bit-rate reduction system.

articleTitle: ISDN Telephone Sets With Advanced Vioce Functions
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed new ISDN telephones which economically provide voice communication and LSIs for ISDN telephones to promote the proliferation of ISDN . These telephones are inexpensive, and provide new services featuring ISDN capabilities in addition to those of conventional telephones. This paper describes the configuration of the telephones and the LSIS which we developed.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Presents the title page of the proceedings record.
